*tex-course*  Reusable course notes template

The template lives at templates/tex-course/ in your Neovim configuration. Copy
it to a new course directory before editing: >sh
    mkdir -p ~/notes
    cp -R ~/.config/nvim/templates/tex-course ~/notes/csce-689
    nvim ~/notes/csce-689/main.tex
<
Edit coursecode, coursetitle, courseterm, and notetaker in main.tex. The default
course is CSCE 689: Algorithms for Data Science; term, author, and lecture date
are explicit placeholders. The paper size is US Letter; change letterpaper to
a4paper in the documentclass options if desired.

Files ~
    main.tex                 Course metadata, title, contents, lecture inputs
    preamble.tex             Packages, theorem environments, numbering, headers
    lectures/lecture-01.tex   Demonstration lecture to replace with your notes
    figures/                 Source figures and images; searched by graphicx
    .gitignore               Generated build files (imported figure PDFs remain
                             trackable)

Writing a lecture ~
Each lecture is a fragment included by main.tex. Start it with: >tex
    % !TeX root = ../main.tex
    \lecture{2}{YYYY-MM-DD}{Concentration inequalities}
    \label{lec:concentration}

    \subsection{Main ideas}
    Your notes here.
<
Use a unique positive lecture number and an explicit date. A lecture starts on
a new page and enters the table of contents. Use subsection/subsubsection for
its internal headings; section is reserved for lecture numbering.

To add another lecture manually, save a file under lectures/ and add its input
line in main.tex before opening the new file in Neovim: >tex
    \input{lectures/lecture-02}
<
The root directive points to main.tex; VimTeX builds main.pdf even when you edit
a lecture fragment. Compile the main document from a shell with: >sh
    cd ~/notes/csce-689
    latexmk -pdf -synctex=1 main.tex
<
With the configured viewer workflow, opening the main file or an included
lecture starts compilation and viewing automatically. Save to rebuild. The
fragments do not compile independently as standalone documents.

Environments and references ~
    theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, claim
    definition, example, exercise, remark
    proof (provided by amsthm; an optional title allows "Proof sketch", etc.)

The numbered environments share one counter within each lecture: Definition
1.1, Theorem 1.2, Example 1.3, and so on. Equations, figures, tables, and algorithms
have their own counters, also reset by lecture. For example: >tex
    \begin{lemma}\label{lem:example}
    A statement.
    \end{lemma}
    \begin{proof}
    A proof.
    \end{proof}

    Lemma~\ref{lem:example}
    Equation~\eqref{eq:example}
<
Use a unique label for each object. latexmk reruns LaTeX as needed for references
and the table of contents. Existing beg + CTRL-K snippets work with these
environment names; the math snippets in |tex-snippets| and |tex-data-science|
work with the preamble's amsmath/amssymb/mathtools packages.

Pseudocode and figures ~
The sample lecture demonstrates algorithm/algorithmic with Require, Ensure,
State, For, and If. Put captions and labels inside algorithm floats, with the
label after the caption. Figures can use paths relative to figures/: >tex
    \begin{figure}[htbp]
        \centering
        \includegraphics[width=0.7\linewidth]{my-figure.pdf}
        \caption{A descriptive caption.}
        \label{fig:example}
    \end{figure}
<
The filename is illustrative; add your own image first. There is no figure
editor integration or lecture-creation command in this template.

Validation ~
The tests copy the template to temporary directories, compile it, check
cross-references and numbering across lectures, and check VimTeX root detection
with the installed plugin (without opening a viewer): >sh
    python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_tex_course.py' -v
<
Primary references ~
    https://castel.dev/post/lecture-notes-3/
    https://www.latex-project.org/help/documentation/amsldoc.pdf
    :help vimtex-multi-file
